\[
P:=\left(\sum x_i\right)\left(\sum\frac1{x_i}\right)\le\left(n+\tfrac12\right)^2.
\]
If n=2, then
\[
P=(1+t)(1+t^{-1})=2+t+t^{-1},
\]
which is greater than \(25/4\) whenever \(t>4\); hence \(t\le4\).

Now assume n\ge3. Keeping x_1=1 and x_n=t fixed, replace any two middle entries u,v by their average c=(u+v)/2. Their contribution to \(\sum x_i\) is unchanged, while convexity of 1/x gives \(1/u+1/v\ge2/c\). Thus this operation does not increase P. Iterating, the minimum occurs at \((1,c,\ldots,c,t)\), with \(1\le c\le t\). For this vector,
\[
P(c)=\bigl(1+(n-2)c+t\bigr)\bigl(1+(n-2)/c+1/t\bigr).
\]
Differentiation shows that its unique critical point is \(c=\sqrt t\), and the derivative is negative before this point and positive after it. Therefore
\[
P(c)\ge f_n(t):=\bigl(1+(n-2)\sqrt t+t\bigr)\bigl(1+(n-2)/\sqrt t+1/t\bigr).
\]
Writing u=\sqrt t, we have
\[
f_n(t)=\left(u+n-2+\frac1u\right)^2,
\]
which is strictly increasing for u>1. At t=4,
\[
f_n(4)=\left(2+n-2+\tfrac12\right)^2=\left(n+\tfrac12\right)^2.
\]
Consequently t>4 would imply \(P>(n+\tfrac12)^2\), a contradiction. Hence t\le4, so \(\max_i a_i\le4\min_i a_i\). ∎

\[

\]
A direct differentiation gives
\[
P'(c)=(n-2)\left(1+\frac{n-2}{c}+\frac1t-\frac{1+(n-2)c+t}{c^2}\right),

whose sign is the sign of \(c^2-t\). Thus P(c) is minimized at c=\sqrt t. Consequently, putting u=\sqrt t,
\[
P\ge\bigl(1+(n-2)u+u^2\bigr)\bigl(1+(n-2)/u+1/u^2\bigr)
=\left(u+n-2+\frac1u\right)^2.
\]

\[
